t:
The Secretary shall take such actions as may be necessary to ensure that—
    (1) minting and issuing coins under this Act result in no net cost to the Federal Government; and 
    (2) no funds, including applicable surcharges, are disbursed to any recipient designated in section 7(b) until the total cost of designing and issuing all of the coins authorized by this Act, including labor, materials, dies, use of machinery, overhead expenses, marketing, and shipping, is recovered by the United States Treasury, consistent with sections 5112(m) and 5134(f) of title 31, United States Code.

fable.w: This is a financial assurance provision directing the Secretary to ensure the commemorative coin program results in no net cost and that surcharges are not disbursed until costs are recovered. The tempting reading is that the mention of a "recipient designated in section 7(b)" brings in an outside party, but that recipient only receives funds and is not consulted on, or given a right to object to, any federal decision. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation, or right to sue.
fable.s: minting and issuing coins under this Act result in no net cost to the Federal Government

opus.w: This section is an internal financial rule: the Secretary must make sure the coin program costs the government nothing overall and must not pay out surcharges until the Treasury has recovered its costs. Mentioning a designated recipient is tempting, but that party only receives money. It is not consulted, does not comment, and has no right to sue or object, so no one outside the government takes part in a federal decision. There is also no rulemaking, hearing, or advisory body.
opus.s: no funds, including applicable surcharges, are disbursed to any recipient designated in section 7(b) until the total cost of designing and issuing all of the coins authorized by this Act
opus.b:
**Step 1: Tempting reading.** The words "recipient designated in section 7(b)" might suggest an outside organization is involved in the coin program. But that recipient only receives surcharge money. It isn't consulted on, and doesn't take part in, any federal decision. This is close to a benefit or grant payout, which the definition excludes. The section only tells the Secretary to keep the program at no net cost to the government and to hold back payouts until costs are recovered. Everyone who acts under it is inside the federal government.

**Step 2: Output.**

qwen_chat.w: This section imposes financial constraints on the Secretary regarding the minting of coins and the disbursement of funds. It does not require the Secretary to consult, coordinate with, or seek input from any outside parties (such as the public, states, or private entities) before making decisions. The 'recipients' mentioned are merely beneficiaries of funds subject to a cost-recovery condition, not participants in the decision-making process. All actors involved in the decision (Secretary, Treasury) are inside the federal government.
qwen_chat.s: The Secretary shall take such actions as may be necessary to ensure that— (1) minting and issuing coins under this Act result in no net cost to the Federal Government; and (2) no funds, including applicable surcharges, are disbursed to any recipient designated in section 7(b) until the total cost of designing and issuing all of the coins authorized by this Act... is recovered by the United States Treasury
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "recipients designated in section 7(b)" are outside parties involved in a decision, but the text only describes a financial condition for disbursing funds to them, not a process of consultation or coordination with them before a decision is made. The decision-making actors here are the Secretary and the Treasury, both inside the federal government.
